questions.q: The acronym **HIV**, which refers to the pathogen responsible for causing AIDS, stands for...
options: Harmful Immune Virus.
Human Infection Vector.
Human Immunodeficiency Virus.
Human Internal Virus.
questions.explain: The acronym stands for **Human Immunodeficiency Virus**. This virus exclusively infects humans and attacks the body's immune system, leading to a deficiency in the body's natural ability to fight off diseases.

questions.q: AIDS is scientifically classified as a **syndrome** rather than a single disease primarily because it...
options: can be permanently cured with modern pharmaceutical antibiotics.
is a collection of various opportunistic infections and symptoms resulting from a compromised immune system.
only affects the human respiratory and digestive organs.
is transmitted exclusively through the consumption of genetically modified foods.
questions.explain: **AIDS** (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) is called a syndrome because it is not just one specific disease. It is a cluster of different symptoms and opportunistic infections (like tuberculosis, pneumonia, and certain cancers) that take advantage of a weakened immune system.

questions.q: Which of the following is a medically proven mode of transmitting the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)?
options: Casual physical contact such as hugging or shaking hands with an infected person
Sharing public toilet seats, swimming pools, or eating utensils
Getting bitten by a mosquito in an environment with high HIV prevalence
The sharing of unsterilized sharp piercing objects like hypodermic needles and razor blades
questions.explain: HIV is transmitted through the direct exchange of infected bodily fluids (blood, semen, vaginal fluids, and breast milk). **Sharing unsterilized sharp objects**, unprotected sexual intercourse, and blood transfusions are primary modes of transmission. HIV is *not* transmitted by mosquitoes or casual contact.

questions.q: The primary physiological effect of the HIV pathogen when it enters the human body is that it...
options: targets and destroys the white blood cells, effectively removing the body's natural defense against diseases.
destroys the red blood cells rapidly, leading to immediate and severe acute anemia.
hardens the major blood vessels, directly causing sudden cardiovascular arrest.
promotes an overproduction of antibodies, resulting in excessive weight gain.
questions.explain: HIV specifically targets the **CD4 cells (a type of white blood cell)**, which play a crucial role in the human immune system. By destroying these cells, the virus strips the body of its ability to combat even minor infections.

questions.q: Which of the following serves as an effective institutional measure to prevent the transmission of HIV?
options: Mixing all donated blood with strong chemical antibiotics prior to human use
Mandating strict laboratory screening and testing of all donated blood before medical transfusion
Ensuring that the blood donor and the receiving patient belong to the same ethnic group
Visually inspecting blood bags for unusual colors or odors before administration
questions.explain: To prevent the transmission of HIV through the healthcare system, it is mandatory to subject all donated blood to **rigorous laboratory screening and testing** before transfusing it into any patient.

questions.q: The unfair discrimination, public shaming, and social rejection of People Living With HIV/AIDS (PLWHA) is known as **stigmatization**. A major negative consequence of this societal practice is that it...
options: legally forces the government to provide free isolation camps for infected individuals.
discourages citizens from voluntarily seeking HIV testing and accessing life-saving antiretroviral care.
naturally cures the virus within the isolated patient due to psychological stress.
forces pharmaceutical companies to reduce the mass production of antiretroviral drugs.
questions.explain: **Stigmatization** creates fear. When society discriminates against those with HIV, individuals become afraid of knowing their status. Consequently, they **avoid voluntary testing and hide their condition**, leading to further spread of the virus and preventing them from receiving necessary medical treatment.
